subject: Word to the wise : rstan-2.8.2 seemingly won't install with StanHeaders-2.9.0. Consequences ?

messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: Word to the wise : rstan-2.8.2 seemingly won't install with StanHeaders-2.9.0. Consequences ?
parts:
Dear list,

I usually use Stan through rstan and rstan often via Sage's version of R. Since  Sage often updates in ways needing recompilation of R and installed packages, I have to reinstall rstan more often tan more "normal" users of this package.

A recent reinstallation failed :

...
** installing vignettes
** testing if installed package can be loaded
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
  impossible de charger l'objet partagé '/usr/local/sage-7.0/local/lib/R/library/rstan/libs/rstan.so':
  /usr/local/sage-7.0/local/lib/R/library/rstan/libs/rstan.so: undefined symbol: _ZN4stan4lang15indexes_grammarIN5boost6spirit17line_pos_iteratorIN9__gnu_cxx17__normal_iteratorIPKcNSt7__cxx1112basic_stringIcSt11char_traitsIcESaIcEEEEEEEEC1ERNS0_12variable_mapERNS9_18basic_stringstreamIcSC_SD_EERNS0_18expression_grammarISG_EE
Erreur : le chargement a échoué
Exécution arrêtée
ERROR: loading failed
* removing ‘/usr/local/sage-7.0/local/lib/R/library/rstan’

I noticed that the "StanHeaders" packages was also installed, at version 2.9.0. So I worked around the problem by desinstalling StanHeaders, reinstalling the 2.0.0 version and reinstalling rstan (successfully).

Hence two questions :
  • What will happen when my next (routine) update of packages rinstall StanHeaders-2.9.0 ? Will this break rstan ?
  • What will happen with the upgrade of BH to 1.60 ? (The previous update broke the installation of rstan...).

Plus, of course, the implicit "when will rstan-2.9.0 be released ?"...

HTH,

--
Emmanuel Charpentier

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: Word to the wise : rstan-2.8.2 seemingly won't install with StanHeaders-2.9.0. Consequences ?
parts: Ben said in another thread rstan 2.9 will be out soon so this is just an issue with CRAN not allowing package releases to be sync'ed with each other.  You submit and then things get through when they get through.  Until then you have to do what you did---use github_install to install a specific version. Not the best but it works.
